segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may not make brine [hilmei] on Shabbat,»

segments.he: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא אֶת מֵי הַמֶּלַח, וְטוֹבֵל בָּהֶן פִּתּוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַתַּבְשִׁיל. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא הוּא הֵילְמֵי, בֵּין מְרוּבֶּה וּבֵין מוּעָט! וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מֵי מֶלַח הַמּוּתָּרִין — נוֹתֵן שֶׁמֶן לְכַתְּחִלָּה לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמֶּלַח.
segments.en: «but one may make salt water and dip one’s bread in it, and place it in cooked food. Rabbi Yosei said: But isn’t it» still «brine, whether» it is «a large quantity or whether» it is «a small quantity? And this is» the type of «salt water that is permitted:» Salt water in which «one places oil initially into the water or into the salt.» This is salt water prepared not in the usual manner.

moves.summary: brine may not be made on Shabbat, but salt water may

moves.summary: permitted salt water: oil placed first into the water or the salt

positions.claim: brine may not be made, but salt water for dipping bread and cooked food may

unresolved.issue: attribution of the closing clause (ואלו הן מי מלח המותרין) to R' Yosei is inferred; the gemara uses it to decide whether R' Yosei prohibits
